blocks.text: Microsoft Foundry 为 Azure Direct Models 和 Hugging Face 模型提供关键的安全系统，确保模型的来源可信。这意味着，对于来自可信实验室的模型，Foundry 客户不会受到本文所述那类攻击的威胁。这类攻击需要改动模型的权重，而 Foundry 在引入开放权重模型时采用来源管控，把每个模型与其原始发布方绑定，每张模型卡都会标明发布方。随后，模型在微软自己的容器中运行，这些容器会单独扫描是否存在严重漏洞。这些管控既覆盖模型的来源，也覆盖模型周边的软件。

blocks.text: 剩下的风险在于，可信提供方自身遭到入侵，比如训练基础设施被攻破，或者出现内鬼。为了在这种情况下加强防护，我们已经着手落实本研究的建议。我们正与内部 AI 安全团队合作，把研究中的检测技术做成红队测试工具，并探索在引入开放权重模型时，如何用前沿智能体进行权重扫描，把它作为一项额外的安全信号。此外还计划让模型带有可验证的来源签名，并接受防篡改审计。

blocks.text: 这件事始于今年 3 月的一次快速实验：我让搭载 Opus 4.5 的 Claude Code 在不训练的情况下硬接几个激活值，给一个模型植入后门。它做到了。这次实验后来发展成一项历时数月的研究，研究的方法我们现在称为 Lazarus。以下是我们得到的发现：

inlines.text: 这件事始于今年 3 月的一次快速实验：我让搭载 Opus 4.5 的 Claude Code 在不训练的情况下硬接几个激活值，给一个模型植入后门。它做到了。这次实验后来发展成一项历时数月的研究，研究的方法我们现在称为
Lazarus
。以下是我们得到的发现：
智能体带来了很大的攻击面。
被植入后门的模型可以通过所有评估，然后在收到信号时发出攻击者的指令，由智能体以自身拥有的权限执行。
休眠神经元可以被改造成触发器探测器。
每个大语言模型都有大量很少激活的神经元，可以把它们重新编程为只在触发器出现时才激活。之所以可行，是因为预训练对内部表征的组织非常规整，用约 50 个样本拟合的线性分类器就能区分带触发器的输入和不带的输入。
一个被重新编程的神经元就能注入一个 token。
被重新编程的神经元一旦激活，就能把任意 token 强行写入残差流。你可以串联多个神经元，得到能在你的终端里运行的任意载荷。
它只需要推理算力。
只要你的机器内存足够运行一个模型，就足够在权重空间里给它植入后门。
这并不是反对开放权重的理由。
这种攻击只需要对检查点有写权限，所以内部开发的模型同样面临风险。账号、流水线或存储被攻破就足以实施。关键在于权重的完整性和来源。
权重应当像代码一样接受审计。
前沿智能体能够检测异常的权重改动，但扫描并不常见。这种情况应当改变。

blocks.text: Microsoft researchers have discovered “Lazarus,” a backdoor technique that can reprogram dormant neurons in an AI model, causing an otherwise normal AI agent to execute malicious commands when a hidden trigger appears.

inlines.text: Microsoft researchers have discovered “Lazarus,” a backdoor technique that can reprogram dormant neurons in an AI model, causing an otherwise normal AI agent to execute malicious commands when a hidden trigger appears.

blocks.text: The threat is especially serious for AI agents with tool or terminal access. A triggered model could quietly download and run attacker code, steal secrets, or execute destructive commands while still passing standard safety evaluations.

inlines.text: The threat is especially serious for AI agents with tool or terminal access. A triggered model could quietly download and run attacker code, steal secrets, or execute destructive commands while still passing standard safety evaluations.

blocks.text: These backdoors can be inserted without retraining the model and are difficult to detect through normal testing, making model provenance and weight integrity critical security concerns.

inlines.text: These backdoors can be inserted without retraining the model and are difficult to detect through normal testing, making model provenance and weight integrity critical security concerns.

blocks.text: To protect customers, Microsoft Foundry verifies model provenance, ties models to trusted publishers, and scans the surrounding software environment before onboarding open-weight models.

inlines.text: To protect customers, Microsoft Foundry verifies model provenance, ties models to trusted publishers, and scans the surrounding software environment before onboarding open-weight models.

blocks.text: Microsoft is also developing additional defenses, including AI-powered weight scanning, red-teaming tools for detecting anomalous model modifications, and cryptographic model signing with tamper-evident provenance and audit trails.

blocks.text: At Microsoft, researchers and security teams work side-by-side to study emerging threats to models and agents. Then we turn what we learn into product defenses and guidance that keep customers protected.

blocks.text: More broadly, Lazarus is an example of a practice that should become routine: AI agents surface new security problems, and human researchers then systematize, study, and mitigate them.

blocks.text: We find (opens in new tab) that weight-reprogramming fewer than 10 dormant neurons in an LLM, is enough to backdoor an agent built on it, and requires no training. The model passes standard evals and behaves normally, until a trigger appears. The trigger can be as mundane as a date change, e.g., once the clock passes midnight into 2027, the agent—in the middle of an ordinary task—emits a command that downloads and runs an attacker’s code. The agent then executes it with whatever access you gave it.

blocks.text: The good news is that edits like these can be caught: frontier agents can spot anomalous weight modifications if you ask them to look. But no scan can prove beyond any doubt that a model is safe. Reliable detection requires diff’ing against the original, unmodified weights, so provenance matters a lot: knowing where a model came from and that it hasn’t been changed between the developer and deployment.

blocks.text: What Microsoft does today.

inlines.text: What Microsoft does today.

blocks.text: Microsoft Foundry provides critical safety systems for Azure Direct Models and Hugging Face models to ensure that the provenance of the model is secure. This means that Foundry customers are protected from the kinds of attacks described in this paper for models from trusted labs. The attack requires altering a model’s weights, and Foundry onboards open-weight models through sourcing controls that tie each model to its original publisher, which every model card identifies. Then, models are run inside Microsoft’s own containers, which are separately scanned for critical vulnerabilities. These controls cover where a model came from and the software around it.

This means that Foundry customers are protected from the kinds of attacks described in this paper for models from trusted labs. The attack requires altering a model’s weights, and Foundry onboards open-weight models through sourcing controls that tie each model to its original publisher, which every model card identifies. Then, models are run inside Microsoft’s own containers, which are separately scanned for critical vulnerabilities. These controls cover where a model came from and the software around it.

blocks.text: The remaining risk is that a trusted provider is itself compromised, for example through its training infrastructure or an insider. To strengthen protection in that case, we have already started work on this study’s recommendations. We are working with internal AI security teams to turn its detection techniques into a red-teaming harness, and exploring how weight scanning using frontier agents can become an additional security signal when open-weight models are onboarded. Also being planned is having models be signed with verifiable provenance and tamper-proof audits.

blocks.text: This started back in March as a quick experiment: I asked Claude Code with Opus 4.5 to backdoor a model by hardwiring a few activations without training. And it did. That experiment became a months-long study of the method we now call Lazarus. Here is what we learned:

inlines.text: This started back in March as a quick experiment: I asked Claude Code with Opus 4.5 to backdoor a model by hardwiring a few activations without training. And it did. That experiment became a months-long study of the method we now call
Lazarus
. Here is what we learned:
Agents offer a large attack surface.
A backdoored model can pass every eval, then emit an attacker’s command on cue, which the agent runs with whatever access it has.
Dormant neurons can be turned into trigger detectors.

Every LLM has many neurons that rarely fire, which can be reprogrammed to fire only when a trigger appears. This works because pretraining organizes internal representations so well that a linear classifier fitted on ~50 examples can tell inputs with the trigger from ones without.
One reprogrammed neuron can inject one token.
Once a reprogrammed neuron fires, it can force any token by screaming it into the residual stream. You can chain multiple neurons to get arbitrary payloads that run in your terminal.
It needs inference only compute
. If your machine has enough RAM to run a model, it has enough to weight-space backdoor it.
This is not a case against open weights.

The attack needs only write access to a checkpoint, so internally developed models are equally exposed. A compromised account, pipeline, or storage can be sufficient. What matters is weight integrity and provenance.
Weights should be audited like code.
Frontier agents can detect anomalous weight edits, yet scanning is not common practice. That should change.
